name: Nauru
system_note: The president is elected by parliament.
snapshot: The world's smallest republic, a single island stripped by phosphate mining, which hosts Australia's offshore asylum processing and now sells citizenship to fund climate plans.
culture: Nauru's 12 clans and Nauruan language anchor identity. Fishing for frigate birds and noddies was a traditional pastime. Australian rules football is the national sport. The island is only 21 square kilometres.
society: Phosphate mining made Nauru briefly one of the richest countries per head in the 1970s, but left most of the island a moonscape, and the money was lost to bad investments. Australia's regional processing centre for asylum seekers is a major source of income. Obesity and diabetes rates are among the world's highest.
situation: David Adeang was elected president in 2023. Nauru switched recognition from Taiwan to China in January 2024 and signed a security and banking treaty with Australia in 2024 that gives Canberra a say over its security deals.
power: A parliamentary republic. The 19-member parliament elects the president, who heads both state and government.
